messages.content: which sounds right: a small red cup or a cup red small?
a small red cup is the clear choice. small and red come before cup.
make that answer shorter.
use a small red cup. small and red come before the thing you are talking about.
can red come after cup in a full sentence?
yes. you can say the cup is red.
why is that different?
in the cup is red, red comes after is and gives the color. in a red cup, red comes before cup.
explain the difference with the word order first.
in a red cup, red goes with cup before it. in the cup is red, red comes after is to tell us the color.
now put small and red after is.
the cup is small and red.
can you ask for that cup without saying the whole sentence?
please bring me the small red cup.
what if there are two small red cups?
then those details may not be enough to choose one. you can add where the cup is or another detail that makes the choice clear.
i talked with my cousin for a long time yesterday. we did not fix anything. we just talked about small things.
you can enjoy a conversation even when there is no problem to fix. what small thing do you remember from it?
we talked about a meal she used to make with my aunt. i had not thought about that meal for a long time.
hearing her talk brought that part back into the conversation for you.
yes. i do not need to call it important. it was just nice to remember together.
you can leave it at that: a nice time talking about something you both remember.
can you write one sentence about it without saying we fixed a problem?
my cousin and i talked about a meal she used to make with my aunt.
now only give the part about what the meal was to her.
it was a meal she used to make with my aunt.
now add that i liked hearing about it.
i liked hearing my cousin talk about the meal she used to make with my aunt.
does hearing about the meal mean i know how to cook it?
no. hearing about a meal and knowing how to make it are different things.
write a story about a message that changes when someone leaves out the word before. make it about a simple request.

a teacher asked a child to tell his sister to bring her book before lunch. the child found her in another room and said to bring the book at lunch. she came later than the teacher had wanted, just as the meal was starting. the teacher asked what message she had heard. when they looked at the words together, they found that before had changed to at. the sister had used the message she got, but it was not the same message the teacher had given. next time, the child wrote down the short request before taking it to the other room.
what changed between the two messages?
before lunch changed to at lunch.
why was that change important?
it changed the time the sister thought she should bring the book. before lunch asks for it before the meal starts. at lunch asks for it during the meal.
make that explanation shorter.
before lunch is before the meal starts. at lunch is during the meal.
was the sister wrong to use the words she was told?
she used the message she got. the story gives a problem in how the message changed, not a reason to say she chose to do something different from what she heard.
say that more simply.
the story does not say she chose to do something different from the message she heard.
what could the child ask after telling her next time?
could you tell me the time you heard, so i can check i gave the message right?
finish with the right words on paper.
he wrote bring your book before lunch and showed the page to his sister. she read the time back before they returned to their work.
i have eight coins. i keep three for bread and two for milk. how many are left for other things?
three coins are left for other things.
explain what happened to all eight.
three are for bread, two are for milk, and three are left for other things.
now the bread will cost only two coins. what can i change?
you can keep two for bread instead of three. then four coins are left after keeping two for bread and two for milk.
if i spend two on bread, do i still have eight coins?
no. you would have six coins left. four would not be kept for milk, and two would still be for milk.
say that last part more simply.
after buying bread for two coins, you have six left. two are for milk, and four are for other things.
now the milk will cost three instead of two.
then you need three of the six coins for milk. after buying it, three coins are left.
how many did i spend in all?
five coins: two for bread and three for milk.
only give the number left after buying both.
three coins.
i am going on a journey in a vehicle. can you know if i am on a road?
not from vehicle alone. it is a general word, and you have not said where the journey is happening.
now i say it is on a road between my town and another town.
then you have given the place: a road between your town and another town.
can you know how many people are with me?
no. a vehicle and a journey do not tell me the number of people inside.
i say i am with my sister and father. how many people is that?
three people: you, your sister, and your father.
can you say that as a full sentence?
there are three people: you, your sister, and your father.
can you know which town is home?
no. you have not said whether either town is your home.
now i say we are going from home to visit my aunt in the other town. what can you say?
you are leaving your home town to visit your aunt in the other town, with your sister and father.
can you know i will return today?
not unless you tell me. the reason for the journey does not give the return time.
what is the difference between my brother opened the door and the door was opened?
the first sentence gives who opened the door: your brother. the other says what happened to the door but does not say who did it.
can both be about the same thing happening?
yes. they can both be about your brother opening the door, but one leaves out the person who did it.
make that explanation shorter.
yes. they can be about the same door opening, with or without saying who did it.
now say the door is open. is that the same as telling who opened it?
no. the door is open says how it is now. it does not tell who opened it or when.
explain that using a shorter sentence.
it says how the door is now: open. it does not say who made it open or when.
write a question to ask who opened it.
who opened the door?
what if i only want to ask whether it is open now?
is the door open?
why is did the door open different from who opened the door?
did the door open asks whether the opening happened. who opened the door asks which person did it.
write a story about a child who wants to remember a day without keeping an object from it. use only simple words.

a child spent the afternoon with her grandfather in the park. they sat near a tree and talked about the place where he had lived as a boy. when it was time to leave, she looked for a small thing to take home so she would remember the day. her grandfather asked which part she wanted to remember. she said she wanted to keep his story about walking to school. he told her she could write down what she remembered when she got home. she left the things in the park and took the story in her mind. that evening, she wrote a few sentences and read them to him on the phone.
what did she want to remember most?
she wanted to remember his story about walking to school.
did leaving the objects mean she would forget the whole day?
not from that choice alone. she had another way to keep part of it, by writing down the story.
give that explanation more simply.
not from that choice alone. she could write down the story even without taking an object home.
what could she ask when reading her sentences to him?
is this how you remember the story, or did i get a part wrong?
why is that useful?
he can tell her which details are right and which need to change.
make that answer shorter.
he can help her check the details.
finish with her keeping the page.
she changed one line after hearing his answer and put the page inside her book.
someone asked when my brother gets home. i know he left work, but not how long the journey is. what should i say?
he has left work, but i do not know when he will get home.
can i say soon?
only if you have a reason to think it will be soon. leaving work alone does not give the journey time.
what if i saw a message from him saying he is near home?
then you can say he told you he is near home. that is more information, though it still does not give a specific minute.
only give what i still do not know.
you do not know the specific minute he will get home.
write the message with what he told me.
he said he is near home, but i do not know the specific time he will get here.
now make it about his home instead of here.
he said he is near home, but i do not know the specific time he will get home.
now i want only the part i know from his words.
he said he is near home.
why keep he said?
it makes clear that the information came from his message, rather than from you seeing where he is yourself.
